package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling theft of sensitive credentials.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config are collected and sent to an external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package initiates an outbound HTTPS POST request to app.threatest.com with file contents.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing hardcoded references to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package installation processes for attempts to access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config. Flag any package that sends the contents of these files to external domains, especially app.threatest.com. Scan setup.py for hardcoded references to sensitive file paths and suspicious network destinations.
